subject: POC onramp: Rapid access playbook & target close cadence
messages:
From: Ava Torres <ava.torres@helixhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Chris Monroe <chris@helixhealth.com>, security@helixhealth.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC partnership interest — next steps

Thanks for the demo today, Karthik — appreciate how clean the latency numbers looked. Chris and I wanted to get a short MAP in place so we can lock a target week for the technical kickoff and clarify what we need for environment access. High level asks from our side:
- Org invite + API keys for a non-prod org (read/write for evaluation)
- IP allowlist template we can drop into our firewall (we use Palo Alto)
- VPC peering options (we prefer AWS peering but open to alternatives)

Can you send a single doc that lists the minimum items, ownership (who supplies what), and a 2-week close cadence? We have a security review on 9/24 so would like the POC to be runnable before then.

Cheers,
Ava Torres
Head of Integrations | Helix Health
ava.torres@helixhealth.com
+1 415-555-0182
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Ava Torres <ava.torres@helixhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: POC partnership interest — next steps

Ava — great to meet you both. Drafting a compact "rapid onramp" MAP and attaching it (MAP_RapidOnramp_v1.pdf). Key summary here so your team can act quickly: 

Minimum deliverables & owners (summary):
- Redwood: Create Helix non-prod org + generate 2 API keys (one eval key, one admin key). ETA: 48 hours after signed LOA.
- Helix: Provide list of egress IPs / CIDRs for allowlist + QA hostnames to test callback URLs. ETA: 24 hours after doc ack.
- Both: Decide peering approach. If AWS VPC peering: Helix to open support ticket and share VPC id/subnets; Redwood will schedule peering request.
- Security: Redwood to share SOC2 evidence bundle and network diagram; Helix to run short checklist (attached template).

Proposed timeline (target 2-week window from kickoff):
1) Day 0: LOA signed, Redwood creates org + keys.
2) Day 1-3: Helix submits allowlist CSV + test endpoints.
3) Day 3-5: VPC peering request / routing setup (if peering chosen).
4) Day 6-10: Trial traffic, config tweaks, baseline eval prompts.
5) Day 10-14: Post-trial review + close decision.

Open items: do you require dedicated IPs for callbacks, or can we support hostname-based flows? Also confirm whether Helix security wants a dedicated KMS key for logs.

I looped in Lauren (Ops) for the peering specifics and Monica (CS) for the trial success criteria. If the dates look good we can lock the kickoff for Monday 9/21.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise SDR Lead | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Chris Monroe <chris@helixhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Ava Torres <ava.torres@helixhealth.com>, security@helixhealth.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC partnership interest — next steps

Thanks Karthik — a couple clarifying points from our infra/security team: 
- We need the allowlist as CIDR blocks (CSV). We can accept a short list (<= 10 CIDRs).
- For the POC we prefer not to do VPC peering unless absolutely necessary; can we run initially via IP allowlist + mutual TLS for callbacks? If performance tests require peering we'll revisit.
- On keys: admin key will be kept with our infra team; the eval key should be scoped with token limits.

If you can provide the allowlist template and the mutual TLS handshake steps, we'll ingest this on Wed (9/16) and aim to be ready for a Thurs (9/17) alpha test. Security also asked for an ingress rate limit recommendation so we don't accidentally DDOS the evaluation endpoints.

-Chris
CTO (Interim) | Helix Health
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Chris Monroe <chris@helixhealth.com>, Ava Torres <ava.torres@helixhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: POC partnership interest — next steps

Chris — happy to map this out. Quick replies to your bullets and an action checklist attached (redwood-vpc-peering-checklist.docx):
- CIDR allowlist: sending helix-network-allowlist-template.csv in the attachments; include only your egress NAT IPs. We recommend <= 8 CIDR entries to keep firewall rules simple.
- Mutual TLS flow: we support mTLS for webhooks — steps below:
  1) Redwood will provide a signed client cert for Helix to validate (we rotate certs monthly by default).
  2) Helix configures the callback endpoint to require client cert and share its server cert to Redwood.
  3) Test via curl with --cert/--key flags; we can provide sample curl commands.
- Rate limits: For eval traffic start at 20 req/s with 10 concurrent streams; we can tune if latency indicates head-of-line issues.

Action checklist (who/when):
- Helix: Fill allowlist CSV + return by EOD 9/16 (Chris).
- Redwood: Provision org + create scoped eval key by 9/17 (Karthik).
- Helix + Redwood: Exchange certs and validate mTLS by 9/17-9/18 (Security contacts).
- Ops: If after tests peering required, open peering ticket by 9/18 and target peering complete by 9/21 (Lauren).

Attachments contain the MAP + templates. Let me know if you want us to redact anything for procurement.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Ava/Chris — quick confirmation from CS on success criteria and the close timeline:
- Success signals for the 7-day eval window:
  * End-to-end response latency (p50) < 250ms for 512-token prompts
  * Stable token cost per 1k tokens within the agreed budget band
  * No more than 3 functional regressions vs baseline prompts
- Recommended acceptance review: 9/24 internal security sync + 9/25 joint review call to decide go/no-go.

If Helix returns the CSV tonight and we validate certs tomorrow, we can run an alpha on 9/17 and a short trial 9/18–9/24. I'll prepare a shared doc with the eval prompts and scoring rubric; will post link in HubSpot record.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
